artists.biography: Beach House is a dream pop duo from Baltimore, Maryland, formed in 2004. The band consists of French-born Victoria Legrand and Baltimore native, Alex Scally. The group's self-titled debut, Beach House (2006), was critically acclaimed. This was followed by its second release, Devotion, in 2008. The band released its third studio album, Teen Dream in January 2010, to critical acclaim and commercial success. Their fourth album, Bloom, was released in 2012 and garnered positive feedback. The band formed in 2004, composed of Alex Scally, who plays the guitar and keyboard, and Victoria Legrand, who sings and plays the organ. Beach House began as a recording project, thus, its music favored simplicity. The band's music consisted largely of the organ, programmed drums, and the slide guitar.

perplexity.description:
Devotion is the second full-length album by Baltimore dream pop duo Beach House, released on February 26, 2008. The record showcases the band's signature ethereal sound, built around an old Yamaha keyboard that served as the primary instrument during recording. Across 11 tracks spanning 44 minutes, the album establishes the atmospheric, melancholic aesthetic that would define the duo's early work, with lead vocalist Victoria Legrand's breathy vocals floating over shimmering synthesizers and minimalist arrangements.

Devotion received critical acclaim comparable to Beach House's debut, establishing the band as significant figures in the dream pop genre. The album debuted at number 195 on the Billboard Chart and was released through Carpark Records. "Gila" served as the first single, while the track "Used to Be" would later be re-recorded and included on their third album, Teen Dream, demonstrating the enduring quality of material from this period.

The album occupies an important position in Beach House's discography as a transitional work that refined their sonic identity before achieving broader recognition with subsequent releases. Its introspective production and carefully crafted soundscapes established the template for their later critical success, particularly with Teen Dream in 2010, which would bring the band to Sub Pop Records and wider acclaim.
